title: Schema-versioned idempotent exports with webhook fanout and dedup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large tenant usage exports sometimes produce duplicate rows when jobs are retried, consumers re-request partial windows, or cross-tenant merges occur. Existing webhook delivery retries and S3 manifest uploads lack a canonical per-row id and schema evolution strategy, making downstream consumers do expensive deduping and schema heuristics.

Objective: Implement a schema-versioned export format with per-row canonical IDs, idempotent reconcile semantics on replay, and a webhook fanout mode that guarantees at-least-once delivery while enabling consumer-side inexpensive dedup using stable export_row_id + export_run_id. Include a cross-tenant dedup helper so merged reports do not double-count usage when customers migrate between tenants or keys.
acceptance_criteria: Export CSV/NDJSON contains export_run_id, export_schema_version, export_row_id columns for every row
Retries of the same export_run_id are idempotent: consumer can safely ingest duplicated files/messages without double-counts
Webhook fanout delivers per-tenant chunks with deterministic partition keys; delivery metadata includes original_file_manifest_url and per-webhook-part export_row_id ranges
Cross-tenant merge flow marks rows with original_tenant_id and canonical_customer_id so downstream dedup logic can identify migrated usage
Documentation and sample consumer script provided for idempotent ingestion and schema-version handling
Metrics: at-least-one delivery latency P95 <= 90s for medium-sized tenants; duplicate ingestion error rate <= 0.1% after rollout
technical_design: Schema versioning: maintain an export schema registry (export_schema_1, export_schema_2) with backward-compatible change rules and transform functions stored in Confluence + a lightweight protobuf mapping stored in S3
Row identity: generate export_row_id = sha256(tenant_id + api_key_id + event_timestamp + event_seq) at export time; include export_run_id UUID for the job
Idempotency: support manifest-level hedging — each export_run has manifest.json listing parts + checksums + row ranges; importers use manifest to dedupe and resume partial imports
Cross-tenant dedup: add original_tenant_id & canonical_customer_id to rows; offline merger service computes canonical_customer_id for tenant migrations and emits mapping file used by importers

Webhook fanout: fanout service pulls CSV parts, streams NDJSON chunks to webhooks (chunk size tunable); uses per-tenant token bucket to enforce rate limits and jittered exponential backoff for failures
Delivery guarantees: at-least-once with unique delivery_id; consumer can acknowledge via webhook callback endpoint to mark as delivered and stop retries
Storage and streaming: use multipart streaming to S3 with 8MB parts, keep manifest for 90 days by default; provide a streaming URL for large consumers
Operational tracing: add correlation_id = export_run_id to all logs, and trace delivery attempts in Console dashboard with token-level cost attribution
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable schema-versioned exports for a small set of internal tenants and 2 customers (1 SaaS, 1 enterprise) for one weekly export; observe ingestion success and duplicate counts
Phase 2 (opt-in): expose new export format behind feature flag in Console; invite early adopters and provide sample import script
Phase 3 (migration): after 3 weeks of stability, migrate existing scheduled exports to new format with a 48-hour parallel window where we produce both legacy and new manifests
Phase 4 (enforce): flip default for new tenants and provide a 30-day opt-out for legacy customers; update SLAs and docs
Rollback: disable webhook fanout and resume previous delivery path by switching export manifest pointer to legacy manifests; past manifests remain readable
testing_notes: Unit tests for export_row_id generation across edge cases (clock skew, duplicate event_seq, unicode keys)
Property tests for manifest generation ensuring part ranges are non-overlapping and cover full row set
Chaos tests: simulate repeated job retries, webhook 5xx spikes, and partial S3 part upload failures; verify idempotent imports
Integration: onboarding test with sample consumer repo that ingests NDJSON via webhook and via S3 manifest, verifying no double-counts
Load test: simulate exports for 10k tenants concurrently to validate token-bucket per-tenant throttling and P95 latency targets
implementation_notes: Backend components: exporter job (Python), manifest generator (Go), webhook-fanout service (Rust), merger helper (Scala) — incrementally swap in new services
Database: store export_run metadata in exports.write DB table with indices on export_run_id and tenant_id
Telemetry: emit metrics export.run.created, export.part.uploaded, webhook.delivery.attempt, webhook.delivery.ack with tags {tenant_id, export_schema_version}
Config: per-tenant rate limits configurable in Console under 'Exports > Delivery Settings'
Security: sign manifest URLs with short-lived tokens; KMS-encrypt export metadata; mark security_review_required
